bookFirst.why: Summit lift slots open about 60 days out and the good times go fast.
Timed tickets sell out, and it’s closed Tuesdays, so plan around that.

tips.head: Get a Navigo Easy card
tips.text: €2, or use the RATP app. Paper tickets are gone. One card per person.

tips.head: From the airport
tips.text: CDG is the RER B. Orly is Metro 14. Both need the €14 airport ticket.

tips.head: Walk it
tips.text: Central Paris is very walkable. Vélib’ is the city bike share.

tips.head: Escalator etiquette
tips.text: Stand on the right, walk on the left.

tipping.note: Service is included in France (service compris), so tipping is optional. Rounding up for great service is a nice extra.

touristTax.title: Tourist tax
touristTax.intro: Paris charges a small tax per adult, per night. Your hotel or rental usually collects it. Pick your stay type to estimate it.
touristTax.rentalNote: Rentals and unclassified stays: 5% of the per-person nightly price, plus add-on taxes (× 3.25), capped at €15.93. Example: €60 a night per person ≈ €9.75 tax.

priceGuide.title: Price guide
priceGuide.intro: 2026 estimates for one adult (non-EU visitor). Edit any price and the whole group sees it.
priceGuide.warning: Prices change, so check before booking.

pocket.title: Pocket Paris
pocket.lede: Phrases, customs and fun facts, sized for your phone.

phrases.title: Phrase guide
phrases.intro: Capital letters show the stressed part. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

items.use: Hello. Every time you walk in somewhere.
After bonjour, never instead of it.

items.say: Je parle un petit peu français
items.sound: zhuh parl uhn puh-TEE puh frahn-SEH

items.say: Une carafe d’eau, s’il vous plaît

items.head: Say bonjour before anything else.
items.text: Entering a shop, café or bakery, or before asking a question.

items.head: Meals are slow on purpose.
items.text: The check won’t come until you ask for it.

items.head: Inside voices.
items.text: Restaurants and the metro are noticeably quiet.

items.head: Tipping isn’t expected.
items.text: Service is included. Rounding up for great service is a nice extra.

items.head: August is quiet.
items.text: Many restaurants close for the whole month.

items.head: Dress is a little polished.
items.text: Comfortable is fine; head-to-toe athletic wear stands out.

items.head: Built to come down
items.text: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World’s Fair and was meant to come down after about 20 years.

items.head: Why the Catacombs exist
items.text: 18th-century cemeteries were overflowing, so bones were moved into old underground quarries.

items.head: Those long, straight boulevards
items.text: They come from Baron Haussmann’s 19th-century redesign, built so monuments sit at the end of the view.

items.head: Notre-Dame is back
items.text: It reopened on December 8, 2024, after the 2019 fire.

items.head: A city shaped like a snail
items.text: The 20 arrondissements (districts) spiral out from the center like a snail shell, so the number tells you roughly how central you are.

activities.title: Eiffel Tower summit
activities.note: Lift all the way to the top. Summit slots go first.

activities.title: Sparkle-hour picnic at Trocadéro or Champ de Mars
activities.note: After dark the tower sparkles for five minutes every hour. Bring a blanket.

activities.title: Louvre
activities.note: Pick two or three must-sees and a meeting spot. It’s enormous.

activities.title: Musée d’Orsay
activities.note: Impressionists in an old train station, plus the giant clock window.

activities.title: Musée de l’Orangerie (Monet’s water lilies)
activities.note: The Water Lilies wrap around two oval rooms.

activities.title: Sainte-Chapelle stained glass
activities.note: Walls of 13th-century stained glass. Best on a sunny day.

activities.title: Musée Rodin sculpture garden
activities.note: The Thinker, rose beds and a bench with your name on it.

activities.title: Notre-Dame
activities.note: Free to visit. Reserve a timed slot to skip the line.

activities.title: Catacombs
activities.note: Tunnels lined with bones, 20 meters underground.

activities.title: Versailles day trip
activities.note: Hall of Mirrors, the gardens and the Trianon. A full day.

activities.title: Montmartre wander + Sacré-Cœur
activities.note: Cobbled lanes, painters on Place du Tertre, and the view from the steps.

activities.title: Le Marais shops + falafel lunch
activities.note: Boutiques and vintage, then falafel on Rue des Rosiers.

activities.title: Canal Saint-Martin aperitif
activities.note: Drinks by the water with the locals at golden hour.

activities.title: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont picnic
activities.note: Hilly park with a little temple on a cliff. Very local.

activities.title: Market morning
activities.note: Cheese, fruit and flowers, then breakfast from the stalls.

activities.title: Cheese and wine tasting
activities.note: Learn your Comté from your Brie with a guided tasting.

activities.title: French cooking or pastry class
activities.note: Macarons, croissants or a market-to-table lunch.

activities.title: Seine cruise (day or dinner)
activities.note: See the monuments from the water. Go at dusk for the lights.

activities.title: Cabaret night
activities.note: Feathers, sequins and a very French night out.

activities.title: Opéra Garnier visit
activities.note: Gilded staircases and a Chagall ceiling.

activities.title: Vintage and secondhand shopping
activities.note: Thrift and secondhand shops all over the city.

bookings.title: Eiffel Tower
bookings.tip: Book 2+ months ahead: summit lift slots open about 60 days out. Stairs tickets also need advance booking. Buy only on toureiffel.paris or from authorized sellers.

bookings.title: Louvre
bookings.tip: Book as soon as your date is released, and at least 2–6 weeks ahead. Closed Tuesdays. Buy only on ticket.louvre.fr or from authorized sellers.

bookings.title: Versailles
bookings.tip: Book several weeks ahead. Timed entry. Closed Mondays.

bookings.title: Sainte-Chapelle
bookings.tip: Book several weeks ahead. Timed entry.

bookings.title: Catacombs
bookings.tip: Book 1+ week ahead; it often sells out. Timed entry only. Closed Mondays.

bookings.title: Musée de l’Orangerie
bookings.tip: Book 1–2 weeks ahead. Morning slots go first.

bookings.title: Musée d’Orsay
bookings.tip: Book several weeks ahead. Timed entry.

bookings.title: Restaurants
bookings.tip: Book 1–3 weeks ahead. Many close for all of August.

bookings.title: Cabaret / cooking class / tastings
bookings.tip: Book 2–4 weeks ahead. Group sizes are limited.

bookings.title: Airport transfer
bookings.tip: Sort it on the day. Needs the separate €14 airport ticket.

itinerary.title: Check in — apartment in Le Marais
itinerary.note: Door code is in the group chat. Fourth floor, no lift, great windows.

itinerary.title: Le Marais shops + falafel
itinerary.note: Falafel on Rue des Rosiers, then wander.

itinerary.title: Sparkle-hour picnic at Champ de Mars
itinerary.note: Bring a blanket. The tower sparkles on the hour.

itinerary.title: Louvre
itinerary.note: Meet under the pyramid 15 minutes early. Pick three must-sees.

itinerary.title: Lunch + a stroll through the Tuileries
Versailles day trip
itinerary.note: RER C to Versailles Château Rive Gauche. Walking shoes!

itinerary.title: Market morning
itinerary.note: Last croissants, plus cheese to take home.

itinerary.title: Check out + airport
itinerary.note: RER B to CDG. Everyone needs the €14 airport ticket.

dream.title: Shakespeare and Company
dream.note: The famous English bookshop across the river from Notre-Dame.

dream.title: Macaron taste-off
dream.note: Pierre Hermé vs. Ladurée. Try both and pick a favorite.

dream.title: Giverny day trip
dream.note: Monet’s house and garden, about an hour from Paris. Spring to fall.

dream.title: Saint-Ouen flea market
dream.note: Vintage everything, just north of the city. Weekends are busiest.

dream.title: Sunset on Pont Alexandre III
dream.note: Gilded lamps and the prettiest bridge photo in Paris.

dream.title: Jazz in a cellar club
dream.note: Latin Quarter caves, for the night nobody wants to go home.

journal.title: The night we booked it
journal.text: Group chat hit 300 messages deciding between Le Marais and Saint-Germain. Noor made a spreadsheet. We ignored the spreadsheet. We picked the apartment with the rooftop view.
journal.favorite: Ava sending “BONJOUR!!” as a voice note at 1am.
